hypothesis: Funding on two venues for the same coin differs because their rate formulas and trader bases differ (Hyperliquid adds a fixed ~11%/yr interest leg; dYdX v4 has its own). Shorting the perp on the richer venue and longing it on the cheaper one is delta-neutral with no spot leg and collects the spread. Rule: per coin, each week, trailing funding spread s = HL - dYdX (annualized, through yesterday); hold short-rich/long-cheap when |s| on capital (|s| x L/2, since both legs post 1/L margin) beats the T-bill yield, else T-bills. Universe: the point-in-time Hyperliquid top 20 intersected with dYdX markets (k-prefixed HL tickers mapped to their dYdX names). Costs: 8bp per leg per trade, daily margin top-up on both legs, liquidation of either leg when the day's high (short leg) or low (long leg) moves 1/L - 3% from the prior close, 5% penalty base with 2% and 10% sensitivities. Sample starts 2024-01-01 to skip dYdX v4's launch period of zero rates. Variants: leverage {2x, 3x} x lookback {7, 30}. PRIMARY, named now: 2x, 30 days. Pass for a defensible out-of-sample 1.5, as with strategy 21: Sharpe after 5% liquidations >= 1.5, PSR(SR>0) >= 0.95, and also >= 1.5 in 2025-26 alone since decay killed the single-venue carry. Also reported: how much of the spread is Hyperliquid's interest constant.
name: crypto cross-venue funding dispersion (Hyperliquid vs dYdX v4)
note: re-declared from edge-audit strategy 25 (declared there at the same time, before any data was pulled); closed there as transferred

FAILS all three declared criteria. primary (2x, 30d) after 5% liquidations: 1.1% excess over T-bills, sharpe 0.39, PSR(>0) 0.71, 2024 sharpe 2.77, 2025-26 -0.36. 3x variants -1.66/-1.73. the raw spread short HL / long dYdX is mostly hyperliquid's 11% interest constant (spread ex-interest -1.6%, -10.6%, -12.6% in 2024/25/26) and decays 9.3% to 0.3% to -1.7%. BUT the rule picks direction and the dispersion it captures is real and persistent: with nothing charged, 6.5% excess and sharpe 3.69, 3.82 in 2025-26. the declared costs eat 5.5 points, split about evenly: switching/entry (8bp/leg) ~2.0, daily collateral top-up ~1.8, liquidation penalty ~1.8. so the gross edge exists and execution cost decides the trade. any cheaper-execution variant designed now has seen this data and is in-sample

hypothesis: Strategy 25 found real Hyperliquid-dYdX funding dispersion (gross Sharpe 3.69, 3.82 in 2025-26) that its declared execution costs consumed. This spec cuts those costs, and it was designed AFTER seeing that breakdown, so its backtest is in-sample and counts for nothing; only the forward record is evidence. SPEC, frozen in models/xv_v1.json with a hash of forward_xv.py: universe = weekly top 20 Hyperliquid perps by trailing 30-day notional that also list on dYdX; signal = trailing 30-day funding spread HL minus dYdX, annualized; 2x leverage on both legs (capital = notional); hysteresis: enter in the spread's direction when |spread| on capital > T-bill + 2%, exit when it falls below T-bill, flip only if it clears the entry band the other way; reviewed weekly at the Monday 00:00 UTC run. Costs: 3bp per leg per trade (resting orders), collateral moves 1bp of the amount moved (daily |return|), liquidation of either leg when the day's high or low moves 47% from the prior close, 5% penalty. Equal capital per universe coin; sleeves not held sit in T-bills. PASS at 52 live weeks: annualized Sharpe of weekly excess >= 1.5 AND PSR(SR > 0) >= 0.95. Interim look at 26 weeks is report-only. KILL: stop and record if cumulative live excess falls below -5% of capital.
name: cross-venue dispersion, forward test (xv_v1)

about: out-of-time test of strategies 20, 21, 24 on BitMEX 2017-2023
rule: Whatever the out-of-time window says is reported as the headline for the bear-market question, including if it is better than the Hyperliquid result. No window trimming: the window is fixed above.
statement: Every carry result so far comes from Hyperliquid, May 2023 onward: no bear market. BitMEX serves perpetual funding since 2016 (XBTUSD) and 2018 (ETHUSD), and spot index prices (.BXBT, .BETH) since 2017. Applying the EXISTING rules unchanged to time before the Hyperliquid sample is an out-of-time holdout for hypotheses already declared, not a new trial. Universe: BTC and ETH perps on BitMEX, equal capital, ETH from its first funding date. Window for the HEADLINE: from the first day with both funding and spot index (2017-03) through 2023-04-30, i.e. strictly before the Hyperliquid sample; 2023-05 onward reported separately for continuity only. Rules, with the exact parameters already declared: strategy 20 always-on carry at 3x; strategy 21 switched (30-day trailing funding vs T-bills, weekly, 3x); strategy 24 equal-weight 2x and its primary (inverse-vol 2x), gate off. Same cost model as validate.py: 8bp per leg, daily margin top-up, liquidation when the day high clears the prior close by 1/L - 3% with a 5% penalty, basis from perp vs spot index closes, T-bills from FRED DTB3. BitMEX XBTUSD and ETHUSD are inverse/quanto contracts; they are modeled as linear USD positions so the rule is tested, not the contract design. Pass for a defensible 1.5: Sharpe after liquidations >= 1.5 over the out-of-time window, and positive excess in each bear year (2018 and 2022) reported as a separate check.

about: out-of-time test of strategies 20, 21, 24 on BitMEX 2017-2023
action: out_of_time.py prints both versions, precommitted first. the corrected one is the result.
verdict: FAILS, and the precommitted headline is wrong because the precommitment was. It modeled BitMEX ETHUSD, a quanto contract settled in BTC, as a linear USD position. A daily-rebalanced short quanto hedged with spot ETH carries a cross-term of -(r_eth x r_btc); over the window that cost 57.8% a year against 57.3% of funding (net -0.5%). The funding was the price of the quanto risk, not a carry, and the as-precommitted Sharpes of 1.59 to 2.15 are that error. Corrected, every spec is about zero (-0.15 to 0.08) and loses money in both bear years (2018 -5% to -10%, 2022 -5% to -8%). BTC alone, the clean inverse contract, gives 0.37 switched and 0.51 at 2x, the same picture as Hyperliquid. The carry does not survive the bear markets it had never seen.

statement: First order-book snapshot, 2026-10-12, for the 16 coins xv_v1 holds in its first live week. Hyperliquid is liquid (median half-spread 0.7bp, ~7bp to take $10k with fees, ~12bp for $100k). dYdX v4 is not: median half-spread 35bp, 42bp to take $10k, 214bp for $100k. dYdX 24h volume is $3m on BTC and under $0.05m on 14 of the 16 coins, with zero trades on XPL and LIT; dYdX open interest is under $0.3m on every held coin except BTC and SOL. Much of the dYdX side of the funding spread is set in markets almost nobody trades. The frozen spec assumes 3bp per leg and has NO capacity filter, so xv_v1 can pass its rule on positions that could not be put on at meaningful size. Recorded now, before any scored week, so that whatever the forward result, it is read together with exec_costs.jsonl. The spec is not changed: changing it would be xv_v2, a new trial.

about: strategy 25/26 capacity: where the gross dispersion came from
statement: Descriptive breakdown, no thresholds chosen, no trials added (capacity.py). Strategy 25 primary held coin-days bucketed by dYdX trailing 30-day average daily volume, known ex ante. Under $0.1m/day: 29% of days, 31% of gross, 13.2%/yr. $0.1-1m: 29%, 25%, 10.6%. $1-10m: 27%, 33%, 15.5%. Over $10m: 15%, 7%, 5.7%/yr, i.e. about T-bills before any cost. Share of gross from coin-days over $1m/day: 59% in 2024, 30% in 2025, 14% in 2026. The median universe coin traded $5.3m/day on dYdX in 2024Q1 and $0.03m in 2026Q4; open interest fell from $0.75m to $0.11m. Conclusion: the dispersion is a limits-to-arbitrage premium that lives in markets too thin to trade; where size is possible it is roughly the risk-free rate. xv_v1 keeps running unchanged as a record, but it is now measuring a spread that cannot be collected at size.

data_window: 2023-06 to 2026-10, plus BitMEX 2017-2023 for the time-series variants
hypothesis: A different mechanism from funding carry, at a frequency where the signal actually changes daily. Crypto returns show momentum at 1-4 week horizons (Liu, Tsyvinski and Wu, JF 2022: a 3-week momentum factor) and reversal at very short horizons, consistent with underreaction and herding in a retail-heavy market. Universe: the point-in-time weekly top 20 Hyperliquid perps by trailing 30-day volume, delisted coins included. Signals use closes through yesterday; positions rebalance at each daily close. CROSS-SECTIONAL: rank on trailing return, long the top third and short the bottom third, equal weight, $1 long and $1 short. TIME-SERIES: each coin long or short its own trailing return sign, $1 gross across the book. Lookbacks: 21 days and 7 days (momentum sign), 1 day (reversal sign). Variants: {cross-sectional, time-series} x {21, 7, 1} = 6. PRIMARY, named now: cross-sectional 21-day. P&L includes hourly funding paid or received on every perp position, and 8bp per side on all traded notional (Hyperliquid measured at ~7bp to take $10k including fees). Collateral earns T-bills, so returns are reported as excess. PASS: Sharpe after costs >= 1.5, PSR(SR>0) >= 0.95, positive Sharpe in both halves of the sample; time-series variants also run on BitMEX BTC/ETH 2017-03 to 2023-04 as an out-of-time check (ETH with the quanto cross-term charged).
name: daily momentum on Hyperliquid perps

note: FAILS 2 of 3 criteria. primary cross-sectional 21-day: gross 58.7%/yr, funding -9.9% (momentum longs the coins that cost most to hold), costs -18.4% at 0.63 turnover a day, net 30.4%. sharpe 0.52 vs bar 3.23, PSR(>0) 0.85; positive in both halves (0.45, 0.65); BTC corr -0.06. but by year +87%, -48%, +123%, -30%, max drawdown 85%: the effect is real and the volatility makes it unusable. 7-day nets -2.0% (costs -31%), 1-day reversal -80.8% (turnover 2.7x a day, costs -78%). time-series variants 0.15 / 0.03 / -0.54. BitMEX BTC/ETH 2017-2023 time-series: 0.49 / 0.46 / 0.45, inconsistent across bear years. momentum exists at 3 weeks in crypto; it is not a 1.5 Sharpe strategy at any of these horizons

hypothesis: Strategy 27's three-week cross-sectional momentum earned 30% a year net but with an 85% drawdown and a Sharpe of 0.52. Momentum strategies crash in high-volatility regimes, and their own recent volatility forecasts future volatility far better than their recent returns forecast future returns (Barroso and Santa-Clara, JFE 2015; Moreira and Muir, JF 2017), so scaling exposure by the inverse of the strategy's own trailing realized volatility should raise the Sharpe. Tried BECAUSE strategy 27 was this volatile, on the same data, so this is post-hoc and its backtest is weak evidence by construction. Rule: strategy 27's primary book (cross-sectional 21-day, top third long / bottom third short, point-in-time top 20 Hyperliquid perps, daily close) multiplied each day by k = target / realized, where realized is the annualized standard deviation of the UNSCALED book's daily net returns over the trailing window through yesterday, target 30% a year, k capped at 2. Scaling changes are traded and pay 8bp per side like everything else; funding scales with the position. Variants: trailing window 30 or 90 days. PRIMARY, named now: 30 days. PASS: Sharpe after costs >= 1.5, PSR(SR>0) >= 0.95, positive in both halves, and max drawdown under 30%. If it passes, it goes to a frozen daily forward test; its backtest alone is not a result.
name: volatility-managed daily momentum on Hyperliquid perps

note: FAILS 3 of 4 criteria, and volatility scaling made it WORSE. primary (30-day vol window): net 11.1%, sharpe 0.35 vs unscaled 0.52, max drawdown 57% vs 85%. 90-day window 13.8%, 0.49, 51%. why: splitting the unscaled book's days by its own trailing volatility, the calm third earns -4%/yr (sharpe -0.09), the middle third -6% (-0.10), the volatile third +110% (1.41). all of crypto momentum's return arrives in its most volatile stretches, the opposite of equity momentum, so scaling down in high volatility cuts exactly the days that pay. the tempting inverse (trade momentum only when volatile) was chosen after seeing this table on this data and is NOT backtested here; it is only honestly testable forward

statement: As of 2026-10-29, six dYdX markets in xv_v1's universe are in FINAL_SETTLEMENT: ENA, LIT, ONDO, VVV, XPL, ZRO (the audit listed five; VVV was never held). forward_xv.py builds its dYdX universe from /perpetualMarkets without checking market status, so it can hold settled markets, whose legs book a spread nobody could trade (dYdX prints rate 0 after settlement, so a short-HL leg collects Hyperliquid funding on paper). Inferred stop times (earlier of the final zero-funding run and midnight after the last traded day): XPL 2026-10-02 and ZRO 2026-10-02, both BEFORE the test began; LIT 2026-10-28; ENA and ONDO 2026-10-29; VVV no trades in 60 days. So XPL (weeks of 10-12 and 10-19) and ZRO (10-19, 10-26) were dead whenever held; ENA and ONDO were live through the two scored weeks and first matter in the week of 10-26. kPEPE maps to PEPE-USD, which is ACTIVE, and the audit's kPEPE point does not reproduce. forward_xv.py is hash-frozen and is NOT changed; a fix would be xv_v2, a new trial. The 52-week verdict will be reported twice: as frozen (forward_xv.py status), and excluding legs on markets that had stopped before the week ended (xv_audit.py, read-only). At this annotation: cumulative -0.031% as frozen, -0.039% ex-settled, over two scored weeks.

Follow-up to the settled-markets annotation above. The stop rule in xv_audit.py was tightened to match ingest_dydx.py: a market counts as stopped only when BOTH its funding has been zero ever since AND it has stopped trading (live dYdX markets print exactly zero about half the time, so a zero run alone proves nothing). Source: docs/AUDIT_2026-10-29.md, finding A3. RETRACTION. This record explains the result with a volatility-tercile split (calm -0.09, middle -0.10, volatile 1.41) and says the inverse rule is only honestly testable forward. That split used pd.qcut over the full sample, so the tercile cutoffs were look-ahead, and the script was never committed. vol_terciles.py now prints both: full-sample -0.09 / -0.09 / 1.39 (the published 1.41 reproduces as 1.39 in the pinned pandas 2.2 env), point in time (expanding rank, at least 180 days) -0.09 / 0.53 / 0.43; the audit got -0.12 / 0.51 / 0.47 with a slightly different ranking. Source: docs/AUDIT_2026-10-29.md, finding A4. deflated_sharpe.py defaults to periods_per_year = 252/5 (weekly, the edge-audit equity convention), but every crypto study passed a MONTH count as n_obs, so every luck bar printed here was about sqrt(50.4/12) = 2.05x too high and every deflated p too low. Corrected (periods_per_year=12; funding_crowding.py, which passes weeks, now uses 52): strategy 25 bar 3.59 -> 1.76 (33 months); 27: 3.23 -> 1.58, DSR 0.008 -> 0.028; 28: 3.27 -> 1.60; the 42-month carry studies 3.07-3.19 -> 1.50-1.56; the crypto-family bar 2.06 -> 1.00 at 19 trials (1.12 at 32). registry.py record now takes --periods-per-year (default 12), and status takes the real sample length instead of the hardcoded 348 weekly observations (which printed 1.108, too LOW for a 3.4-year sample; now 1.557 at 42 months). No verdict flips with the liquidation and settled-market corrections in place. Two results move: strategy 24's primary (holdout 1.24 after liquidations) now beats the crypto-family bar, with deflated p 0.66 at 19 trials (first printed 0.23), not significant; and strategy 21's uncharged 1.92 would have cleared the corrected bar of 1.56, which only the liquidation correction (0.72) prevents.
